_disclaimer: IMPORTANT: All rules in this file are ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLES created for demonstration purposes only. They do NOT represent actual policies of any bank, RBI, NPCI, Visa, Mastercard, or any other financial institution or regulator.

policies.title: Failed Payment – Amount Debited
policies.rule_text: If a customer's account is debited but the merchant's system does not show a successful payment, the transaction may be in a 'pending reversal' state. Under standard interbank settlement protocols (illustrative), the amount should auto-reverse within 3–5 business days. If not reversed, the customer may raise a dispute with supporting evidence.
evidence_required: Screenshot or SMS showing account debit
Merchant order/transaction failure screenshot
Bank transaction ID or UPI reference number (UTR)
Date and approximate time of transaction
Merchant name and order ID (if available)
policies.escalation_threshold: If not resolved in 7 business days

policies.title: Duplicate / Double Debit
policies.rule_text: When the same amount is debited multiple times for a single transaction intent, the excess debit(s) are considered erroneous. The customer is entitled to a reversal of the extra charge(s). The bank or payment processor must investigate within the prescribed timeline (illustrative: 10 business days) upon receipt of a formal dispute with evidence.
evidence_required: Bank statement showing both/all debits
Transaction reference IDs for each debit
Merchant receipt or order confirmation (if only one order exists)
Date, time, and amount of each debit
Merchant contact or support ticket number (if raised)
policies.escalation_threshold: If not resolved in 10 business days

policies.title: Unauthorized Transaction
policies.rule_text: If a customer reports a transaction they did not authorize, the case is classified as a potential fraud event. The customer must report the incident immediately to the bank's fraud helpline and block the affected instrument. Under illustrative zero-liability provisions, customers who report promptly and did not contribute to the fraud through negligence may be eligible for a full reversal after investigation.
evidence_required: Transaction alert SMS or email
Customer declaration that the transaction was not authorized
Date and time the customer became aware of the transaction
Confirmation that card/UPI/credentials were not shared with anyone
Police FIR or complaint number (for high-value cases)
Any suspicious calls or messages received prior to the incident
policies.resolution_timeline: 7–10 business days for provisional credit; final resolution up to 45 days (illustrative)
policies.escalation_threshold: Immediate escalation if transaction > ₹50,000 or if card is compromised

policies.title: Missing UPI Transaction Reference (UTR)
policies.rule_text: Every successful UPI transaction generates a Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) number. If a customer cannot locate a UTR but their account was debited, the transaction may be in a pending or failed state. The bank's core banking system must be checked against the NPCI settlement records (illustrative). Disputes without a UTR require the bank to trace the transaction using account details and timestamps.
evidence_required: Account debit confirmation (SMS or bank statement)
Approximate transaction date and time
Destination UPI ID or account number
Transaction amount
UPI app name used (e.g., GPay, PhonePe, Paytm)
policies.escalation_threshold: If transaction remains unresolved after 7 business days

policies.title: Merchant Service Dispute – Product or Service Not Received
policies.rule_text: When a customer pays for goods or services that are not delivered or rendered, the transaction may be disputed as a 'services not rendered' or 'merchandise not received' case. For card transactions, this may qualify for a chargeback under the applicable card network rules (illustrative). For UPI payments, resolution depends on merchant cooperation or escalation to the payment aggregator.
evidence_required: Payment confirmation and order receipt
Expected delivery date
Evidence of non-delivery (e.g., delivery tracker screenshot, merchant non-response)
Communication with merchant (chat logs, emails)
Merchant name, website, and order ID
Date payment was made
policies.escalation_threshold: If merchant does not respond within 7 business days

policies.title: Refund Credited to Wrong Account
policies.rule_text: If a refund is initiated by the merchant but the customer does not receive it, the funds may have been credited to an incorrect or expired account. The bank must verify the beneficiary account details used in the refund transaction (illustrative). If an error is confirmed, the misdirected credit must be recalled and re-credited to the correct account within the prescribed timeline.
evidence_required: Merchant refund confirmation with refund reference number
Customer's correct bank account or UPI ID
Original transaction details
Bank statement showing the refund was not received
Date refund was supposed to be processed
policies.escalation_threshold: If refund not received 15 business days after merchant confirmation

policies.title: Escalation to Ombudsman / Regulatory Body
policies.rule_text: If a complaint remains unresolved for more than 30 days after being filed with the bank, or if the customer is unsatisfied with the bank's final response, the customer may escalate to the Banking Ombudsman under the RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (illustrative reference only). Filing is free of charge and can be done online. The Ombudsman can award compensation up to the prescribed limit.
evidence_required: Proof of complaint filed with the bank (complaint/ticket number)
Bank's response or rejection letter (if any)
All original transaction evidence
Timeline of events and communications
Customer's contact details and account information
policies.resolution_timeline: Ombudsman typically resolves within 30 days of receiving complete complaint (illustrative)
policies.escalation_threshold: After 30 days of unresolved bank complaint

policies.title: EMI / Subscription Charge Dispute
policies.rule_text: Customers who cancel a subscription or EMI mandate may still be charged if the cancellation was not processed before the next billing cycle. For NACH (National Automated Clearing House) mandates (illustrative), the customer may request a 'stop payment' instruction via their bank. For recurring card charges, the customer may request reversal of the charge and cancellation of the stored credential with evidence of prior cancellation.
evidence_required: Proof of subscription/mandate cancellation (email, screenshot)
Date of cancellation
Bank debit transaction details
Merchant name and subscription plan details
Previous billing history (optional, helpful)
policies.escalation_threshold: If charged again after confirmed cancellation
